record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: To prove universality for the centered and scaled stopping-time variable associated with the Toda eigenvalue algorithm, can one control jointly, as n→∞, the statistics of the relevant extreme eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvector components for β=1 invariant ensembles and for β=1 or β=2 Wigner ensembles?

evidence.quote: In order to prove universality for the centered and scaled variable T(1)−⟨T(1)⟩/σT(1) ... for β = 1 invariant ensembles, and for β = 1 or 2 WE’s, this problem is still very much open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random real symmetric (β=1) or complex Hermitian (β=2) matrix drawn from one of the following ensembles:
(i) a β=1 invariant ensemble, with density proportional to $\exp(-n\,\mathrm{tr}\,V(M))\,dM$ on real symmetric matrices, for a suitable confining potential $V$; or
(ii) a Wigner ensemble with β=1 (real symmetric) or β=2 (Hermitian), whose entries above the diagonal are i.i.d. centered random variables of variance $1/n$, with sufficient moment conditions.

Apply the Toda flow / QR-type eigenvalue algorithm to $M_n$: this produces a sequence of isospectral tridiagonal matrices $M_n(t)$ that converges as $t\to\infty$ to a diagonal matrix of the eigenvalues, with the largest eigenvalue appearing in the top entry. For a fixed tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, define the stopping time
$$T^{(1)}_n(M_n)=\inf\{t\ge 0: |M_n(t)_{12}|<\varepsilon\},$$
i.e. the first time the off-diagonal entry adjacent to the top-corner eigenvalue falls below $\varepsilon$. Let $\langle T^{(1)}_n\rangle$ denote its mean and $\sigma_{T^{(1)}_n}$ its standard deviation.

Question: Prove that the centered and rescaled stopping time
$$\frac{T^{(1)}_n - \langle T^{(1)}_n\rangle}{\sigma_{T^{(1)}_n}}$$
converges as $n\to\infty$ to a universal limiting distribution (independent of the underlying ensemble within the above classes). The principal analytic obstacle is to obtain joint control, as $n\to\infty$, of the statistics of the extreme (edge) eigenvalues of $M_n$ together with the corresponding eigenvector components (in particular the first component of the top eigenvector), in the cases of β=1 invariant ensembles and of β=1 or β=2 Wigner ensembles.
artifact.category_tag: Random matrix theory and eigenvalue algorithms
artifact.status_search_result: Universality for the Toda halting time has been proven for the largest eigenvalue computation in the Hermitian (β=2) Wigner case (Deift–Menon–Olver–Trogdon and follow-up work, e.g. arXiv:1604.07384), using joint control of edge eigenvalue and eigenvector statistics via delocalization, rigidity and edge universality. The β=1 invariant case and β=1 Wigner case require the analogous joint edge eigenvalue–eigenvector control, which is more delicate; based on available sources the full statement for β=1 invariant ensembles and β=1 Wigner ensembles in the form posed appears to remain partially open, although significant components (edge universality, eigenvector delocalization for symmetric Wigner) are now available.

status_evidence.title: Universality for the Toda algorithm to compute the largest eigenvalue of a random matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes universality for the halting time of the Toda algorithm computing the largest eigenvalue, using rigidity, delocalization and edge universality.
status_evidence.claim: Universality of the Toda stopping time has been established for certain ensembles (notably β=2 Wigner), via joint edge eigenvalue/eigenvector control.

status_evidence.title: Universality for Eigenvalue Algorithms on Sample Covariance Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Extends universality results for halting times of eigenvalue algorithms to further ensembles.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has extended universality for halting times of related eigenvalue algorithms, but full β=1 invariant/Wigner cases remain delicate.

status_evidence.title: Eigenvector Distribution of Wigner Matrices (Knowles–Yin)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides eigenvector distribution and delocalization results for Wigner matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The eigenvector-component statistics required as input have been established for Wigner ensembles.
